observations.text: Rating did not know whether the immersion suit is donned with or without a lifejacket.
Engine officer was not aware of the safety inspection checklist; the checklist was not ship specific and did not mention risk assessment for hot surfaces in the engine room.
Cargo watchkeeper could not say what device is used to deal with static charge during STS operations.
Master's answers on the personnel transfer basket and its certification were not satisfactory.
Rating could not answer questions on enclosed space entry procedure and precautions.

positives: Deck officer gave detailed familiarisation and was aware of company procedures.
Rating was aware of MOB and recovery of person from water procedures, better than normal.
Engine room well maintained with proper housekeeping.
style: Gets deep into paperwork and documentation.
Compares dates and data against company checklists.
Asks many questions to ratings and junior officers.

questions.q: What are the ISPS security levels?
What is the company procedure for near miss reporting?
What is the drug and alcohol policy?
Where do you muster in case of emergency?
Does the MOB drill report mention the Williamson turn procedure?
Show the drill report for the last boat lowered in the water.
Show the last bunker samples landing receipt, BDN, Oil Record Book and EEDI certificates.
Is the immersion suit in the forward store donned with or without a lifejacket?
Show the certification for the personnel transfer basket.
During STS, what device is given to deal with static charge?
As duty officer, what action do you take in case of a master riser fire?
What is the working principle of the ballast water treatment system?
What are the D2 standards for ballast water?
What is the enclosed space entry procedure and what precautions are taken?
What action do you take if you see a man overboard?
Show the log book, bell book, STS checklist, latest chart updates and Nav warnings in force.
Show the last passage plan and digital publications.

checks.item: All certificates checked with master and PMS reviewed
Risk assessment for mooring winch brake testing
Familiarisation for new joiners compared with joining dates and company checklist
Drill matrix as per SMS and drill reports
Lifeboat boarded, rudder hard over to hard over tested, lifeboat air pressure checked
Life rafts and HRU expiry checked
Forward liferaft emergency lights and packing of the box checked for water ingress
Personnel transfer basket and its certification checked
Helicopter equipment and SCBA bottle pressure for helicopter fire fighting checked
Manifold photographed, bunker manifold valves and flanges checked
High level and overfill alarms tried out
Pumproom visited, COP, TRO pump and AUS system photographed, bilge alarms tried out
Garbage record book, ballast record book, last ODME test and last P/V valve pressure test checked

tips: Make sure ratings can explain immersion suit use with and without a lifejacket.
Train ratings on SIMOPS and static charge precautions during STS.
Keep the safety inspection checklist ship specific and include hot surface risk assessment.
summary: SIRE 2.0 inspection by Capt. Suresh Menakath at Lome, Togo on a vessel engaged in STS operations. The inspector was calm but went deep into paperwork and documentation, questioning ratings and junior officers closely. Result was 3 positive and 3 negative remarks.
